story: My boss promised my unpaid September 2026 salary of Rs 20,000 on WhatsApp. Do I need a Section 65B certificate to use the chat as proof?

timeline.event: Boss promised to pay unpaid salary
timeline.user_words: My boss promised my unpaid September 2026 salary of Rs 20,000 on WhatsApp.

facts.user_goal: To understand if a Section 65B certificate is required to use the WhatsApp chat as legal proof of the salary promise.
missing: Whether the boss actually paid the salary after the promise

rules.name: monthly_due_date
rules.message: Wages for September 2026 were due before the end of 07 October 2026 (the 7th of the next month).
rules.label: When wages were due

rules.name: wage_claim_limitation
rules.message: File your wage claim before 07 Oct 2029 (1064 days left). This counts 3 years from 07 Oct 2026 (when September 2026 wages fell due; each later month has its own, later deadline). Don't wait for the last date.
rules.label: Last date to file your wage claim

rules.name: where_to_claim
rules.message: You (or your union) can file a claim before the wage authority. For banks, railways, telecom, mines, insurance and central PSUs this is the Central Government's authority; for other employers it is your State labour department. It can order up to ten times the claim as compensation and recovers unpaid amounts like land revenue. The employer has to prove they paid you.
rules.label: Where to claim

rules.name: amount
rules.message: Unpaid wages: 1 month(s) x Rs 20,000 = Rs 20,000 (before any lawful deductions; HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment).
rules.label: Amount

answer.summary: Your boss owes you Rs 20,000 for September 2026. The wages were due before the 07 October 2026. You can file a claim with the labour authority within 3 years (before 07 October 2029). The authority can order up to ten times the claim as compensation. The boss must prove they paid you. Your WhatsApp chat can be used as evidence. A certificate is required to submit electronic records like your WhatsApp chat as evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

support.text: Your boss must pay your September 2026 wages of Rs 20,000 before the 07 October 2026.
support.reason: The law text requires monthly wages to be paid before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month (e.g., September wages before 7 October 2026). The sentence states 'before the 07 October 2026' which is correct for September wages, but the law text does not specify a particular date like '07 October 2026' - it only says 'before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month.' However, the sentence's date is consistent with the rule. Actually, re-reading: the law says 'before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month' which means by the 7th day (not before the 7th). The sentence says 'before the 07 October 2026' which would mean before October 7, i.e., by October 6. This is a stricter requirement than the law. The law allows payment up to and including the 7th day. So 'before 07 October' is more restrictive than 'before the expiry of the seventh day.' Therefore false.

support.text: The unpaid wage claim must be filed before 07 October 2029.
support.reason: The law text states that claims must be filed within three years from the date the claim arises, with possible extension for sufficient cause. It does not specify '07 October 2029' as a deadline. The sentence adds a specific date that is not in the law text.

support.text: The labour authority can order up to ten times the claim as compensation.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states: 'the payment of compensation in addition to the claim determined, which may extend to ten times of the claim determined.'

support.text: The boss must prove they paid you.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states: 'the burden to prove that the said dues have been paid shall be on the employer.'

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your offer letter, salary slip, or the company's registered office on the MCA website (mca.gov.in).
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(1)-(4) (Time limit for payment of wages); Code on Wages, 2019, s.45(1)-(6) (Claims authority, compensation, recovery and time limit); Code on Wages, 2019, s.59 (Burden of proof on employer); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(d) (Central or State Government: whose authority applies); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(y) (main part, clauses (a)-(j)) (What counts as "wages")
